title: Noah
lead: The righteous man who "walked with God" (Genesis 6:9), built the ark, and became the father of all later humanity through Shem, Ham and Japheth. Jewish law derives the seven laws for all nations from God's commands to him.

sections.b: Noah's name is explained by "relief" (Genesis 5:29) and plays on "rest" and "favor" (6:8; 8:4, 21). He is the tenth from Adam. After the flood he becomes a farmer and the first vintner, and his drunkenness leads to the curse on Canaan (9:20–27). Ezekiel names him among the most righteous of men (Ezekiel 14:14, 20); Isaiah recalls "the waters of Noah" (Isaiah 54:9). Luke lists him among Jesus' ancestors (Luke 3:36). Hebrews 11:7 and 2 Peter 2:5 call him an heir and preacher of righteousness. The rabbis taught seven "laws of the children of Noah" binding on all people (Talmud, Sanhedrin 56a).
